objectives.knowledge: Classify clinical genetic tests across the human lifespan (Diagnostic, Predictive, and Perinatal: Pre-implantation, Prenatal, Newborn) and distinguish PGT-A, PGT-M, and PGT-SR (P12).
objectives.application: Outline the IVF procedure (hormonal stimulation, in vitro fertilisation, embryo biopsy & transfer), Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing (NIPT after 10 weeks), and Invasive Prenatal Testing (CVS 11–14 wks vs Amniocentesis >15 wks) including maternal DNA contamination checks.
objectives.evaluation: Analyse the clinical role, timing, advantages, and limitations of diagnostic, predictive, pre-implantation (PGT-M), non-invasive (NIPT), and invasive prenatal testing in Ben's Huntington's disease case study context (M7).

terminology.def: Umbrella category spanning genetic testing around conception, pregnancy, and birth: Pre-implantation (IVF embryos), Prenatal (during pregnancy: NIPT, CVS, Amniocentesis), and Newborn screening.

Three subtypes of Pre-implantation Genetic Testing on single cells biopsied from early IVF embryos: PGT-A (Aneuploidy/chromosome count), PGT-M (Monogenic single-gene disorders like HD), and PGT-SR (Structural Rearrangements).

Assisted reproduction where hormones stimulate multiple egg release, eggs and sperm are fertilised outside the body, and selected healthy embryo(s) are transferred to the uterus (does not always implant; may cause multiple births).
A safe blood test taken from the mother's arm after 10 weeks gestation to analyse cell-free fetal DNA (cffDNA) for chromosomal mutations and targeted DNA mutations.

Invasive ultrasound-guided prenatal tests sampling placental chorionic villi (CVS, 11–14 weeks) or amniotic fluid (Amniocentesis, after 15 weeks) to test fetal DNA — often paired with maternal DNA to rule out maternal contamination.

theoryPoints: Hospital Tests to Genetic Testing Taxonomy: Broad hospital diagnostics (imaging, biochemistry, haematology, microbiology, genetics) narrow into three genetic testing pillars — Diagnostic (confirming symptomatic illness), Predictive (assessing asymptomatic risk), and Perinatal (Pre-implantation, Prenatal, Newborn).

Lifespan Timing of Genetic Testing: Egg & sperm join → Pre-implantation genetic testing (before uterine implantation) → Prenatal genetic testing (during pregnancy) → Newborn genetic screening (at birth) → Diagnostic & Carrier/Predictive testing (adulthood).

Pre-implantation Genetic Testing (PGT-A, PGT-M, PGT-SR) & IVF: Egg (23 chr) + Sperm (23 chr) → Zygote (46 chr) → divides to 2, 4, 8 identical cells → single cell removed without harming embryo → tested for genetic disease (PGT-M for single-gene HD; PGT-A for aneuploidy; PGT-SR for structural rearrangements) → only unaffected embryos transferred to uterus. IVF requires hormone stimulation, external fertilisation, and embryo transfer (caveats: implantation not guaranteed; risk of multiple births).

Non-Invasive vs Invasive Prenatal Testing: NIPT uses a maternal arm blood sample after 10 weeks to detect placental cell-free DNA (chromosomal & selected DNA mutations, zero miscarriage risk). Invasive testing uses ultrasound-guided Chorionic Villus Sampling (CVS, 11–14 weeks, placental sample) or Amniocentesis (after 15 weeks, amniotic fluid sample); a sample of the mother's DNA may be required to ensure tested DNA belongs exclusively to the fetus.

Case Study Alignment (P12 & M7): Molecular PCR diagnostic testing confirms symptomatic Ben's HD; for Ben's current pregnancy, invasive CVS/amniocentesis gives definitive diagnosis (weighed against miscarriage & termination ethics) whereas NIPT is screening-focused; for future pregnancies, IVF + PGT-M selects unaffected (hh) embryos without termination.

steps.label: Step 1 — Symptomatic Adult (Ben → P12 Diagnostic)
steps.detail: Ben has involuntary chorea; a molecular diagnostic test (targeted PCR sizing CAG repeats in HTT exon 1) confirms Huntington's disease (≥40 repeats = full penetrance).

steps.label: Step 2 — Current Pregnancy (Wife → M7 NIPT vs Invasive CVS/Amniocentesis)
steps.detail: After 10 weeks, NIPT offers a zero-risk maternal blood screen (best established for chromosomal aneuploidies/selected mutations), while definitive fetal HD diagnosis requires invasive ultrasound-guided CVS (11–14 wks, placenta) or Amniocentesis (>15 wks, amniotic fluid), using maternal DNA control to rule out contamination.

steps.label: Step 3 — Future Pregnancies & Existing Children (M7 IVF + PGT-M vs Predictive Deferral)
steps.detail: For future family planning, IVF combined with PGT-M biopsies a single cell from early 8-cell/blastocyst embryos and transfers only unaffected (hh) embryos (avoiding termination, though implantation is not guaranteed and multiple births may occur). Predictive testing for Ben's 6yo & 3yo is deferred until adulthood (age 18).

hingeQuestions.question: Which subtype of Pre-implantation Genetic Testing (PGT) would specifically be used during IVF to screen embryos for Huntington's disease (a single-gene disorder on chromosome 4)?
options: PGT-A (Aneuploidy screening for extra/missing whole chromosomes)
PGT-M (Monogenic / single-gene disorder testing targeting the HTT CAG expansion)
PGT-SR (Structural rearrangements such as reciprocal translocations)
hingeQuestions.explanation: PGT-M targets monogenic (single-gene) inherited conditions like Huntington's disease or cystic fibrosis, whereas PGT-A checks whole chromosome copy number (aneuploidy) and PGT-SR checks structural chromosome rearrangements.

hingeQuestions.question: Why may clinicians also collect a sample of the mother's DNA when performing Chorionic Villus Sampling (CVS) or Amniocentesis?
options: Because fetal cells do not contain any chromosomes before week 20
To verify that the DNA analysed from the placental or amniotic fluid sample genuinely comes from the fetus and is not contaminated by maternal cells
To stimulate egg release for an IVF cycle
Because ultrasound scanners cannot locate the placenta without maternal blood
hingeQuestions.explanation: Maternal cell contamination (MCC) can skew invasive prenatal results; comparing maternal DNA markers against the CVS/amniocentesis sample confirms that the diagnostic result belongs strictly to the fetus.

plenary: Genetic testing spans the entire human lifespan: Pre-implantation (PGT-A/M/SR via IVF) → Prenatal (NIPT >10 wks; Invasive CVS 11–14 wks & Amniocentesis >15 wks) → Newborn screening → Adult Diagnostic & Predictive testing.
PGT removes a single cell from an early IVF embryo without harming development so only unaffected embryos are implanted — though IVF implantation is not guaranteed and can result in multiple births.

Invasive CVS and amniocentesis use ultrasound guidance to test fetal DNA (with maternal DNA verification to prevent contamination), giving learners the exact clinical depth required for OCR P12 and M7.
